hints.title: Parse Tree Overhead Obstacle
hints.text: Parsing the string into separate hierarchical syntax trees is unnecessary overhead. How can a single numeric counter tracking open brackets determine the peak nesting depth in one pass?

hints.title: Peak Counter Invariant
hints.text: Nesting depth increases on every '(' and decreases on every ')'. The maximum depth ever reached by the counter equals the maximum nesting depth of the string.

hints.title: Single Counter Tracking Procedure
hints.text: Initialize curr_depth and max_depth to 0. For each character in s: if '(', increment curr_depth and update max_depth with max(max_depth, curr_depth); if ')', decrement curr_depth. Return max_depth.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 100)
complexity.notes: Single pass with a scalar depth counter.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Building recursive parse tree data structures allocates unnecessary objects and takes excess memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining running integer state requires zero heap allocation and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that characters other than '(' and ')' have no effect on depth.
